headline: Speed is distance over time—how fast you're going depends on both what you cover and how long it takes
universal_truth: Speed isn't just about moving fast; it's about the relationship between distance and time; efficiency matters
fun_facts: Light travels at 670,616,629 mph—the universal speed limit
A snail moves at about 0.03 mph; a cheetah at about 70 mph
The speed of sound varies—it's faster in water than in air, and even faster in steel
discussion_questions: Are you moving fast enough toward your goals?
When is speed helpful and when is it harmful?
What would 'faster' look like in an area you care about?

hook.script: A cheetah moves at 70 mph. Light moves at 670 million mph. Speed is how much distance you cover in how much time. It's the ratio that matters—not just distance, not just time, but their relationship.

cliff.script: We often focus on how far we've gone or how long we've worked. But speed combines both. What does thinking about speed reveal?
cliff.prompt: Why does speed matter as a concept?

options.text: Speed reveals efficiency—how much progress per unit time—which helps you compare approaches and optimize how you achieve goals
options.response: Yes. Speed = Distance / Time. Two people can travel the same distance but at different speeds. Two approaches can require the same effort but produce different speeds of progress.
Sometimes, but speed has costs—accuracy, depth, sustainability...

fact1.title: The Speed Formula
fact1.script: Speed equals distance divided by time. To go faster, cover more ground—or do it in less time. Both levers work. Sometimes efficiency gains are easier than effort increases.

fact2.title: Speed vs Velocity
fact2.script: Speed is how fast; velocity includes direction. You can be moving fast but in the wrong direction—high speed, wrong velocity. In life, make sure you're going fast toward the right destination.

fact3.title: Sustainable Speed
fact3.script: Sprint speed and marathon pace are different. Maximum speed isn't sustainable. Finding the speed you can maintain matters more than occasional bursts. Sustainable speed beats fast burnout.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Speed isn't just moving fast—it's the relationship between distance and time. Check your direction, find sustainable pace, and optimize for speed that lasts.

outro.script: That's Day 223. Tomorrow, we'll explore acceleration—speeding up and slowing down. Until then, evaluate your speed toward one goal.

growTrack.title: Speed Check - Progress Per Time
growTrack.activity: Pick a goal. How much progress have you made in the last month? Is that speed sufficient to reach your goal in your timeframe? Could you go faster by working differently (not just harder)? Speed is about efficiency, not just effort.
